title: Started r/INATAI, a place to find teams for AI-assisted game dev
author: Significant-Neck-520
selftext:
​

Every so often I see someone here say how cool it would be to get a bunch of people together, pool our subscriptions, and see what we could make with an ungodly amount of tokens. Then those threads go quiet. I've never gotten an answer on them, and by now I can't even find them to DM anyone.

So instead of asking whether something like that already exists, I went ahead and made it: r/INATAI. It's based on r/INAT (I Need A Team), but for people who use AI in their workflow. I'm not sure what INAT's official stance on AI is, but given the backlash we get pretty much everywhere, I never risked posting an AI-focused team search there.

I've never run a Reddit community. I was looking for this kind of place, not planning to manage one. But I could already see the "why don't you make one yourself?" comments coming, so here we are.

If you're looking for collaborators, or have a project that needs people, come post there. And if you know of an existing place that already does this, please let me know, I'm really interested in one.

Also, a brand-new sub with almost nobody in it isn't the most useful place yet, and this sub has way more reach. So if you're looking for people or a team, feel free to reply right here too.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Good idea, but why would we need a team? My team is Gemini, Claude and Codex.

replies.author: Significant-Neck-520
replies.body: Ahh, thats a fair take,  but tokens are limited. And direction is still required, playtesting, etc. My last project has several areas implemented already and I couldnt playtest them all. Anyway, building a team is a very complex task, I understand the positives of working alone

replies.author: kytheon
replies.body: Tokens are cheaper than humans. By a very large margin. But go for it, honestly I wouldn't mind sharing the burden with other ai devs. You do the art, I handle the game design and Greg does the coding.
